cards.text: This psalm doesn't name its writer, but it opens with "The LORD reigns" as an announcement to the whole world. THREE WORDS, friend, the shortest headline in history, and it STILL covers everybody on the planet. And the very next line tells the nations how to take it.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD reigns, so the psalm tells the nations to sit back and relax.

cards.text: He's enthroned above the cherubim, and the psalm says, "let the earth quake!" Friend, the biggest shake-up of my whole life was somebody yanking the junk drawer open looking for TAPE.

cards.question: The psalm says the LORD is great in Zion. How high does it say He is exalted?

cards.text: But shaking isn't the whole response. The psalm calls for praise too, "Let them praise Your great and awesome name—He is holy!" and then it says, "The mighty King loves justice."

cards.question: True or false: The psalm says the mighty King loves justice but hasn't acted on it yet.

cards.text: Loving justice is one thing, but this King puts it into practice. He has established equity and exercised justice and righteousness in Jacob, the man God renamed Israel (Gen 32:28).
Then the call goes out: "Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at His footstool; He is holy!" There's that line again.

cards.question: Now the psalm reaches back into Israel's history. Which two men does it name among the LORD's priests?

cards.text: That's Moses, Israel's leader, and his brother Aaron (Exod 4:14). Then one more name: Samuel, the prophet who anointed Saul and David (1 Sam 10:1; 16:13), among those who called on His name.

cards.question: True or false: When Moses, Aaron and Samuel called to the LORD, the psalm says He answered.

cards.text: He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud. Friend, I nearly hop clean off my gold base when the oven timer dings, and these men got a whole PILLAR OF CLOUD.

cards.question: The LORD spoke from the pillar of cloud and gave them decrees and statutes, and they ___ them.
The psalm talks right to God about these same men. How does it describe Him toward them?

answers.text: Forgiving yet an avenger of their misdeeds
Forgiving so He overlooked their misdeeds
Strict so He never forgave their misdeeds

cards.question: True or false: Because God was forgiving to them, the psalm says their misdeeds didn't matter to Him.

cards.text: One last call to exalt the LORD our God. Earlier it was worship at His footstool, but this time the place is different.

cards.question: Earlier the psalm called people to worship at His footstool. Now it calls them to worship at His holy ___.

cards.text: And the very last words: "for the LORD our God is holy." That's three times this psalm says He's holy, friend, and when something shows up THREE times, it's not a line anymore, it's the WHOLE RECIPE.

findings.problem: The appositive "Jacob, the man God renamed Israel" makes "in Jacob" sound as though Psalm 99:4 locates God's justice in the individual patriarch. Here Jacob refers to Israel collectively; Genesis 32:28 supports the renaming but not that identification.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Saying "There's that line again" relies on the earlier occurrence of "He is holy!" in verse 3, but the card cites only verse 5.

rule.text: The gold base is part of him. He can hop, jump and dive face-first into the chocolate chips, but the base always comes with him. He never steps off it or leaves it behind.
